deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

location.description: The location for the management server (management console)
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description: The name of management server (management console)
name.rationale: Name has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: even without manual ID configuration ID will be automatically generated.

type.description: The type of management server (management console). Default value: "BACKUP_RESTORE" Possible values: ["BACKUP_RESTORE"]
type.rationale: Type has no impact on the security of the resource or data contained.

networks.description: Network details to create management server (management console).

networks.network.rationale: The selected VPC network defines the security boundary and connectivity scope for the management server, but not writing a policy in T1/2026.

networks.peering_mode.description: Type of Network peeringMode Default value: "PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS" Possible values: ["PRIVATE_SERVICE_ACCESS"]
networks.peering_mode.rationale: Peering mode controls how the management server connects to Google services and affects the security posture of the network connection, but not writing a policy in T1/2026.
